claim: Caenorhabditis elegans halts postembryonic growth and development shortly after hatching in response to monomethyl branched-chain fatty acid (mmBCFA) deficiency.
source_text: Caenorhabditis elegans halts postembryonic growth and development shortly after hatching in response to monomethyl branched-chain fatty acid (mmBCFA) deficiency.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript and references to previous work (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008).

claim: d17iso-glucosylceramide is a critical metabolite in regulating growth and development in C. elegans.
source_text: an mmBCFA-derived sphingolipid, d17iso-glucosylceramide, is a critical metabolite in regulating growth and development.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that disrupting d17iso-GlcCer biosynthesis causes developmental arrest and genetic suppression experiments.

claim: The d17iso-glucosylceramide lipid function is mediated by TORC1 in the intestine.
source_text: this lipid function is mediated by TORC1 and antagonized by the NPRL-2/3 complex in the intestine.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by genetic experiments showing TORC1 activation bypasses lipid deficiency and tissue-specific rescue experiments.

claim: The d17iso-glucosylceramide lipid function is antagonized by the NPRL-2/3 complex in the intestine.
source_text: this lipid function is mediated by TORC1 and antagonized by the NPRL-2/3 complex in the intestine.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by data showing nprl-3(ku540) mutation suppresses lipid deficiency-induced arrest and RNAi experiments.

claim: The essential lipid function is bypassed by activating TORC1.
source_text: Strikingly, the essential lipid function is bypassed by activating TORC1 or inhibiting NPRL-2/3.
evidence_reasoning: Directly demonstrated by experiments showing TORC1-activating transgenes rescue mmBCFA-deficient animals.

claim: The essential lipid function is bypassed by inhibiting NPRL-2/3.
source_text: Strikingly, the essential lipid function is bypassed by activating TORC1 or inhibiting NPRL-2/3.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by nprl-3(ku540) mutation and nprl-2/3 RNAi experiments rescuing lipid-deficient animals.

claim: TOR complexes sense various nutrient signals including amino acids, energy, and growth factors.
source_text: While amino acids, energy, and growth factors have been described as nutrient inputs to TOR complexes, roles of lipid molecules as signals to these systems in controlling postembryonic growth and development were not known.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from the literature cited (Ma and Blenis, 2009; Laplante and Sabatini, 2012; Zoncu et al., 2012).

claim: Roles of lipid molecules as signals to TOR complexes in controlling postembryonic growth and development were not known prior to this study.
source_text: While amino acids, energy, and growth factors have been described as nutrient inputs to TOR complexes, roles of lipid molecules as signals to these systems in controlling postembryonic growth and development were not known.
evidence_reasoning: This represents a gap in knowledge that the authors identify based on literature review.

claim: When hatched in food-free surroundings, C. elegans enters a quiescent state termed L1 diapause.
source_text: When hatched in food-free surroundings, this nematode enters a quiescent state, termed L1 diapause
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge cited from previous studies (Johnson et al., 1984; Munoz and Riddle, 2003; Baugh and Sternberg, 2006).

claim: An insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling (IIS) pathway plays a critical role in the induction of L1 diapause.
source_text: An insulin/IGF-1 receptor signaling (IIS) pathway plays a critical role in the induction of L1 diapause and survival of the developmentally arrested animals
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from multiple cited studies (Gems et al., 1998; Baugh and Sternberg, 2006; Kniazeva et al., 2008; Lee and Ashrafi, 2008; Jones et al., 2009; Soukas et al., 2009).

claim: TOR complexes play prominent roles in regulating postembryonic growth and lifespan in C. elegans.
source_text: Moreover, TOR complexes have also been indicated to play prominent roles in regulating postembryonic growth and lifespan in C. elegans
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from cited literature (Vellai et al., 2003; Syntichaki et al., 2007; Hansen et al., 2008; Honjoh et al., 2009; Lucanic et al., 2011).

claim: Monomethyl branched-chain fatty acids (mmBCFAs) are widely present in bacteria, plants, and animals, including humans.
source_text: Monomethyl branched-chain fatty acids (mmBCFAs) are widely present in bacteria, plants, and animals, including humans
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from cited studies (Nicolaides and Ray, 1965; Ran-Ressler et al., 2008).

claim: In mammals, mmBCFAs are derived from branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs).
source_text: In mammals, mmBCFAs are derived from branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from cited studies (Morii and Kaneda, 1982; Oku et al., 1994).

claim: The physiological roles of mmBCFAs are essentially unknown.
source_text: The physiological roles of these FA variants are essentially unknown, even though they were found to be present at very high levels in certain tissues
evidence_reasoning: This represents a gap in knowledge identified by the authors based on literature review.

claim: In C. elegans, mmBCFAs C15ISO and C17ISO are synthesized from the BCAA leucine.
source_text: In C. elegans, readily detectable mmBCFAs C15ISO and C17ISO are synthesized from the BCAA leucine
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited previous work (Kniazeva et al., 2004).

claim: The key enzymes in mmBCFA synthesis pathway in C. elegans, including BCKDC, ELO-5, and ACS-1, are evolutionarily conserved.
source_text: The key enzymes in this de novo synthesis pathway, including the branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase complex (BCKDC), an FA elongase (ELO-5), and an acyl CoA synthetase (ACS-1), are evolutionarily conserved
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited studies (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008) and represents established knowledge.

claim: Newly hatched C. elegans that are deficient for mmBCFAs cannot initiate postembryonic growth and development, and instead enter L1 diapause.
source_text: We have previously shown that newly hatched C. elegans that are deficient for mmBCFAs cannot initiate postembryonic growth and development, and instead enter L1 diapause.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the authors' previous work (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008).

claim: The developmental arrest caused by mmBCFA deficiency is independent of the IIS pathway.
source_text: Further genetic analysis suggested that this developmental arrest is independent of the IIS pathway
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by cited previous work (Kniazeva et al., 2004, 2008).

claim: In mmBCFA-deficient elo-5(−) larvae, the amount of mmBCFA-containing sphingolipids were dramatically reduced.
source_text: We found that in mmBCFA-deficient elo-5(−) larvae, the amount of mmBCFA-containing sphingolipids were dramatically reduced
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: d17iso-sphinganine (d17iso-SPA) is sufficient to overcome elo-5(−) L1 arrest.
source_text: This purified d17iso-SPA fraction, but not a chemically synthesized c17iso-sphingolipid with a straight-chain d18:1-LCB or a straight-chain LCB d16-SPA, was found to be sufficient to overcome elo-5(−) L1 arrest

claim: d17iso-SPA suppresses L1 arrest at a much lower concentration than C15ISO or C17ISO.
source_text: We observed that d17iso-SPA suppressed the L1 arrest at a much lower concentration than C15ISO or C17ISO
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by dose-response experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Low concentrations of d17iso-SPA suppress L1 arrest without restoring mmBCFA levels.
source_text: we observed that the low concentrations of d17iso-SPA suppressed the L1 arrest without restoring mmBCFA levels
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by gas chromatography data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Supplementation with d17iso-SPA, but not mmBCFAs, suppresses the L1 arrest phenotype caused by feeding RNAi of sptl-1.
source_text: we found that supplementation with d17iso-SPA, but not mmBCFAs, also suppressed the L1 arrest phenotype caused by feeding RNAi of sptl-1
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: mmBCFAs promote postembryonic development through d17iso-SPA.
source_text: We thus conclude that mmBCFAs promote postembryonic development through d17iso-SPA.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on multiple lines of experimental evidence including rescue experiments and metabolic analysis.

claim: fath-1(RNAi)-treated animals cause larval arrest.
source_text: Both fath-1(RNAi)-treated animals (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1) and the cgt-1(−);cgt-3(−) double mutant (Marza et al., 2009) cause larval arrest.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experimental observations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The cgt-1(−);cgt-3(−) double mutant causes larval arrest.
source_text: Both fath-1(RNAi)-treated animals (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1) and the cgt-1(−);cgt-3(−) double mutant (Marza et al., 2009) cause larval arrest.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data and cited previous work (Marza et al., 2009).

claim: The arrest caused by fath-1(RNAi) or cgt-1(−);cgt-3(−) double mutant could not be overcome by feeding d17iso-SPA.
source_text: We found the arrest under either condition could not be overcome by feeding d17iso-SPA
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: d17iso-glucosylceramide (d17iso-GlcCer) may be the lipid molecule that mediates the role of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in promoting postembryonic growth and development in C. elegans.
source_text: These results suggest that d17iso-glucosylceramide (d17iso-GlcCer) (Figure 1A) may be the lipid molecule that mediates the role of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in promoting postembryonic growth and development in C. elegans.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from genetic epistasis experiments showing that disrupting GlcCer synthesis cannot be rescued by d17iso-SPA.

claim: The ku540 mutation permits mmBCFA-depleted C. elegans to bypass L1 arrest and propagate continuously.
source_text: Mutation ku540 permits mmBCFA-depleted C. elegans to bypass L1 arrest and propagate continuously
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experimental data showing elo-5(−);ku540 animals reach adulthood without mmBCFA supplementation.

claim: elo-5(−);ku540 animals did not restore mmBCFA levels.
source_text: Mass spectrometry (MS) and gas chromatography (GC) analyses indicated that elo-5(−);ku540 did not restore mmBCFA levels
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by MS and GC data shown in Figure 2D-G.

claim: elo-5(−);ku540 animals did not restore d17iso-sphingolipid levels.
source_text: Mass spectrometry (MS) and gas chromatography (GC) analyses indicated that elo-5(−);ku540 did not restore mmBCFA levels, and consequently the levels of d17iso-sphingolipids
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by MS data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: elo-5(−);ku540 animals had ceramides and glucosylceramides containing straight chain d16LCB rather than d17isoLCB.
source_text: In contrast to wild type animals, elo-5(-);ku540 animals had ceramides and glucosylceramides containing straight chain d16LCB rather than d17isoLCB

claim: The suppression of L1 arrest by the ku540 mutation is neither due to a change in mmBCFA nor the metabolism of the derived sphingolipids.
source_text: These data indicated that the suppression of L1 arrest by the ku540 mutation is neither due to a change in mmBCFA nor the metabolism of the derived sphingolipids.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on MS and GC data showing no restoration of mmBCFAs or d17iso-sphingolipids.

claim: ku540 renders mmBCFAs nonessential for C. elegans development.
source_text: Therefore, our data suggest that ku540 renders mmBCFAs nonessential for C. elegans development.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from data showing ku540 suppresses mmBCFA deficiency without restoring mmBCFA levels.

claim: The L1 arrest caused by RNAi of fath-1 is effectively suppressed by ku540.
source_text: We found that the L1 arrest under both conditions, just like the arrest caused by elo-5(−), was effectively suppressed by ku540

claim: The L1 arrest caused by mutating both cgt-1 and cgt-3 is effectively suppressed by ku540.
source_text: We found that the L1 arrest under both conditions, just like the arrest caused by elo-5(−), was effectively suppressed by ku540

claim: d17iso-GlcCer mediates the roles of mmBCFAs and d17iso-SPA in postembryonic development.

evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from genetic epistasis experiments showing ku540 suppresses defects in GlcCer biosynthesis.

claim: ku540 bypasses the requirement of mmBCFAs and d17iso-GlcCer in development by modifying a regulatory function downstream of d17iso-GlcCer.
source_text: our biochemical and genetic data indicate that ku540 bypasses the requirement of mmBCFAs and d17iso-GlcCer in development and does so by modifying a regulatory function downstream of d17iso-GlcCer.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on genetic epistasis and biochemical data showing ku540 acts downstream of lipid biosynthesis.

claim: ku540 is a loss-of-function missense mutation of nprl-3.
source_text: ku540 is a loss-of-function mutation of nprl-3
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by genetic mapping, sequencing, and complementation experiments.

claim: The ku540 mutation changes a conserved glycine at position 60 to glutamic acid in NPRL-3.
source_text: The ku540 mutation changes a conserved glycine at position 60 to glutamic acid

claim: NPRL-3 is conserved in all eukaryotes.
source_text: NPRL-3 is conserved in all eukaryotes

claim: nprl-3(RNAi) mimics the effect of the ku540 mutation in rescuing the L1 arrest phenotype caused by blocking mmBCFA or glucosyl-ceramide biosynthesis.
source_text: C. elegans images showing nprl-3(RNAi) mimics the effect of the ku540 mutation in rescuing the L1 arrest phenotype caused by blocking mmBCFA or glucosyl-ceramide biosynthesis.

claim: RNAi of nprl-2 also suppresses the developmental arrest of elo-5(−) larvae.

claim: NPRL-2 and NPRL-3 in C. elegans may function in a complex to negatively impact mmBCFA/d17iso-GlcCer-mediated L1 growth.

source_text: The NPR2/3 complex was proposed to be a negative regulator of the TOR pathway in S. cerevisiae
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from cited work (Neklesa and Davis, 2009).

claim: Reducing raga-1 or rheb-1 activity reverses the rescue effects of nprl-3(ku540) on elo-5(−) mutant background.
source_text: While nprl-3(ku540) effectively suppressed the L1 arrest phenotype of elo-5(−), the suppression dramatically decreased when raga-1(RNAi) or rheb-1(RNAi) were applied to the elo-5(−) nprl-3(ku540) double mutant

claim: The rescue effect of nprl-3(ku540) on elo-5(−) depends on intact TORC1 activity.

claim: The effects of raga-1(RNAi) and rheb-1(RNAi) in reversing nprl-3(ku540) suppression were essentially eliminated by C17ISO supplementation.

claim: elo-5(−) nprl-3(ku540) animals treated with ife-2(RNAi) or rsks-1(RNAi) yielded results similar to those obtained with raga-1(RNAi) and rheb-1(RNAi).

claim: TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer and is negatively regulated by NPRL-3.

claim: Constitutive activation of TORC1 is sufficient to overcome the L1 arrest of mmBCFA-deficient animals.

claim: TORC1 acts downstream of d17iso-GlcCer to promote L1 growth and development.

claim: The intestinal d17iso-GlcCer/TORC1 pathway regulates postembryonic growth.

claim: TORC1 activation by mmBCFA/d17iso-GlcCer is essential in the intestine of L1 larvae and cannot be effectively compensated by another leucine/TORC1 mechanism in C. elegans.
